content: WASF1, also referred to as Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein family member 1 or WAVE1 (WASP-family verprolin homologous protein 1), is a protein encoded by the WASF1 gene in humans. The protein encoded by the WASF1 gene belongs to the Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein (WASP) family. It plays a pivotal role downstream of Rac, a small GTPase from the Rho family, by participating in the WAVE regulatory complex. This complex is essential for regulating the actin cytoskeleton, which is required for processes such as membrane ruffling. WASF1 has been demonstrated to associate with the actin nucleation core Arp2/3 complex. This interaction enhances actin polymerization in vitro, indicating its critical role in actin dynamics. Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is a disorder of the immune system, and it is believed to arise from defects in the regulation of the actin cytoskeleton. WASF1 has been shown to interact with BAIAP2 (Brain-specific angiogenesis inhibitor 1-associated protein 2) and Profilin 1, further highlighting its involvement in actin cytoskeleton regulation and cellular processes.
